articles.title: Toronto Tempo win WNBA draft lottery and No 1 pick with JuJu Watkins in play
articles.summary: Expansion team beat 33% odds to claim top pick. Houston Comets will select second in 2027 draft. USC star Watkins could be available at No 1. The Toronto Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery on Sunday, securing the No 1 pick in the 2027 draft and potentially the chance to select Southern California…
body: The Tempo, who joined the league as an expansion team this past season, entered the lottery tied with the Houston Comets for the best chance of landing the top pick. Both teams had a 33% chance of winning.
Washington had the third-best chance of landing the No 1 pick, holding the Chicago Sky’s first-round selection through a trade. The Mystics stayed at No 3.

Seattle will select fourth, followed by the Portland Fire at No 5. The Los Angeles Sparks will pick sixth and seventh, having acquired the latter selection in a trade with Phoenix. New York, Dallas, Indiana and Chicago follow, with the Sky also holding the 12th pick. Dallas, Golden State and Minnesota round out the first round.

The draft pool remains uncertain after the NCAA granted players a fifth year of eligibility. Players have until 2 April to declare for the draft, with those competing in the Final Four given additional time.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton urges F1 to ‘push harder and move faster’ on diversity
articles.summary: Former champion calls for more equality in recruitment. ‘Inspiration means nothing without opportunity’ Lewis Hamilton has demanded Formula One does more to deliver on diversity and inclusion, warning that the future of the sport is dependent on taking robust action to address inequality in…
body: Hamilton has called on F1 to make greater investments, more extensive recording and publishing of data of who is in the sport and a commitment from teams to guarantee a number of paid early-career places for young people from underrepresented backgrounds.

Hamilton’s Mission 44 foundation established in 2021 has published a new report, titled Igniting Inclusion, five years after the groundbreaking assessment made by the Hamilton commission to investigate and address the lack of representation of black people, women and those from lower‑income backgrounds in motorsport.
The new review demonstrates F1 still has much work to do, the seven‑time world champion insists.

“Formula One is inspiring millions of young people around the world but inspiration means nothing without opportunity,” Hamilton said. “We can’t tell young people to dream big and then not open the doors when they try to make those dreams a reality.

articles.title: Greaves out of Grand Slam despite win over Zonneveld
articles.summary: Beau Greaves' win over Niels Zonneveld is in vain as she is knocked out of the Grand Slam of Darts because of Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
body: Beau Greaves was eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts at the group stage despite ending her campaign with a win over Niels Zonneveld in Wolverhampton.
Greaves, 22, beat Dutchman Zonneveld 5-3 but it was not enough to keep her in the competition after Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
The three-time women's world champion fought back impressively from 3-1 down, winning three consecutive legs to take the lead in the best-of-five match.
She missed two match darts in a tense final leg but 28-year-old Zonneveld could not capitalise, failing to take out 154 before Greaves finished with double eight to seal the victory.

articles.title: Tuchel hails England’s statement win over Spain as ‘complete performance’
articles.summary: England top Nations League group after 3-2 win with 10 men. Tuchel: ‘What a performance we put out there’ Thomas Tuchel hailed England’s 3-2 Nations League win over Spain at the Eastadio Metropolitano as a statement result and the best performance of his tenure.
body: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the spot and when Nico Williams pulled another goal back, England were forced to hang on. They got a memorable victory over the line thanks to a series of stunning James Trafford saves; the best was the double stop in added time to deny Fermín López and then Aymeric Laporte.

England advance to the Nations League quarter-finals as the group winners having leapfrogged Spain, who had lost only once in their previous 43 matches – the penalty shootout defeat against Portugal in the 2025 Nations League final.

Tuchel was asked whether it was the best performance of his time in charge. “Yes,” he said. “Given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. That was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

“What a performance we put out there to be deservedly 3-0 up after 60-65 minutes. Of course the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes [of defending] against Spain in Spain feels like three hours!

articles.title: Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final
articles.summary: Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset. Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds. Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title. After a week dominated by a headline-grabbing stadium imbroglio, Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to the vital…
body: Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volley off the crossbar and in to seal a 2-1 upset that shattered Gotham FC’s bid for the league’s first-ever treble. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the NWSL Shield and in-season Challenge Cup winners into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit.

On a windswept afternoon where unyielding gusts undercut the warmth of a near-cloudless 50F sky, a physical opening stretch produced six fouls in the first eight minutes before either side threatened. Gotham recorded the first shot after 12 minutes when Jaedyn Shaw ran onto a Guro Reiten pass and missed wide right. Kansas City answered three minutes later, with Malawian star Temwa Chawinga firing wide left from the center of the area.

articles.title: LeBron James now third in all-time NBA assists
articles.summary: LeBron James had 11 assists and moved into third on the NBA's career list, as he added 15 points and six rebounds to lead the Philadelphia 76ers past the Indiana Pacers 131-124 on Sunday.
body: James, who turns 42 next month, dished one to VJ Edgecombe in the fourth quarter for assist 12,092 to pass Jason Kidd on the career list. John Stockton and Chris Paul are No 1 and 2 in NBA history.
James continued an early habit in his first season with the Sixers in picking his spot to take control of a game.

This one came in the third quarter, right after Sixers fans went wild when seldom-used 7-foot-6 center Tacko Fall checked into the game. James immediately went to work picking apart the Pacers and scored eight straight points to give them an 82-73 lead.

Fall helped in that pivotal third quarter stretch for James. Fall grabbed an offensive rebound that led to a possession where James would sink two from the free-throw line. James then added a near-uncontested driving layup because of a perfect screen from Fall. James added a 20-footer and a dunk during the run.

articles.title: After 140-plus years, Wesleyan and Trinity make NCAA Division III football playoffs for first time
articles.summary: Both Wesleyan and Trinity have been playing college football for more than 140 years. Trinity first played in 1877. Wesleyan's first organized team played in 1881. On Sunday, both added to their long and impressive histories by earning bids to the NCAA Division III playoffs for the first time.
body: Trinity, Wesleyan and Amherst finished in a three-way tie for the NESCAC championship at 8-1. All three earned berths to the 40-team Division III playoffs.

Wesleyan, which scored 24 unanswered points to defeat Trinity 27-20 on Saturday to force a three-way tie for the NESCAC championship, will play host to Springfield on Nov. 28 at noon in the second round.

Trinity, which earned the NESCAC's automatic berth by means of a coin toss, will play host to Rensselaer (8-2) on Saturday at noon. Amherst will play host to Bridgewater State on Saturday, also at noon.
Wesleyan has won three-straight NESCAC championships and four overall. Trinity has won 13, the most in NESCAC history.

articles.title: Is Trafford England's new No 1 after Spain heroics?
articles.summary: Do England have a new No 1? Thomas Tuchel insists not. "There's no No 1," he said. But Jordan Pickford might have his work cut out to wrestle the shirt back from James Trafford on the evidence of his performance in England's 3-2 win over Spain.
body: James Trafford made a string of impressive saves to help England claim a 3-2 win over Spain in the Nations League; Leeds goalkeeper was picked ahead of Jordan Pickford at the Metropolitano Stadium, so is he Thomas Tuchel's man now?

It felt significant that he started in the first place. Pickford has been England's undisputed first choice for a decade; an outstanding servant to the national team whose total of 94 caps puts him behind only Peter Shilton among the most-capped goalkeepers.

But this was undoubtedly England's biggest test of their Nations League campaign and Tuchel opted for Trafford, encouraged by his displays at home to Spain and away to Czech Republic in September. "He had a brilliant match," he added afterwards.

If it is a changing of the guard, then it is being handled carefully. "I think it's smart management," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane before kick-off in Madrid. "This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."

articles.title: Louisville WBB leaves UConn's Geno Auriemma at loss for words in blowout
articles.summary: Louisville women's basketball 's 69-51 win over UConn left Geno Auriemma at a loss for words. It took the Huskies' head coach 87 minutes after the Nov. 15 game to make his way to the podium, where he addressed how he thought his team performed.
body: "We were stunned in the locker room at some of the stuff that we saw today," Auriemma said.

Louisville came out of the gates aggressive. The Cards grabbed the first points of the night and never looked back against a team that normally looks to take advantage of its opponents and their moments of weakness.

But there was never really a stretch where anyone at the KFC Yum Center thought they were going to watch the Cards slowly lose the double-digit lead they maintained the whole game, and that caused Auriemma to remain silent the longer it went on.

Louisville pushed UConn to the point where he didn't want his team to have a break. He didn't want to stop the game and have the Huskies regroup. Auriemma left Louisville with the same amount of timeouts he entered the Bluegrass State with.

articles.title: Cowboys Prized Rookie Captures Attention After Being ‘Trucked’ on TD
articles.summary: Last week was, arguably, the best game in the young career of Dallas Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs, as he logged two passes defensed–including a game-sealing interception–and a sack in a win over the Colts on the road.
body: But the idea that the NFL is a week-to-week league is not just an empty cliche spouted by coaches because while the No. 11 pick from the 2026 NFL draft was riding high after the Colts win, he had a much different experience against the 39ers in Week 10 at home. Downs was repeatedly targeted by the 49ers in coverage and, worse, he was on the down side of one of the most impressive plays of the game–a 25-yard touchdown run by fellow rookie Kaleon Black.

On the play, Black took the ball on a pitch from 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy and got downhill immediately. He was five yards upfield when Downs–known for his hard-hitting style of play at Ohio State–stepped up to meet him. But as Downs lowered himself for the tackle, Black lowerd his shoulder and simply ran over Downs, leaving him in his wake. Black pushed through Cobie Durant, too, for the score.
All in all, it is safe to say Downs will not be rookie of the week this time around. The reaction was swift.
From 49ers reporter David Lombardi: “Kaelon Black gave Caleb Downs a welcome-to-the-NFL moment even though he himself is also new to the NFL.”

Clayton was the second seed to be eliminated on Sunday after 15th-seed Luke Woodhouse lost 5-1 to Krzysztof Ratajski.
In the final match of the afternoon session, eighth seed Josh Rock knew he could not afford to lose three legs to Kevin Doets, but he ultimately lost the match 5-3.
And in the evening session, sixth seed Smith beat Gabriel Clemens 5-4, but conceded too many legs and exits the tournament following Saturday's shock loss to Rusty-Jake Rodriguez.

articles.title: England talking points: Tuchel learns Argentina lesson as full-backs shine
articles.summary: After England beat Spain in their own back yard in a statement result, we look at the main talking points from a memorable moment in Madrid...
body: England beat Spain 3-2 in a statement performance and result in Madrid; the Three Lions ended the world champions' 43-game unbeaten run to top their Nations League group and be a seeded team for the quarter-finals in March; Sky Sports look at the main talking points from the big result...

England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.
They snapped into tackles and gave short shrift to their opponents when they called for fouls. It was physical, it was aggressive. It was certainly not England trying to replicate the Spanish style.

The set-piece routine for the second goal was a reflection of how those phases have risen in importance in the Premier League and fittingly saw two Arsenal players combine to score it. Then, when down to 10 men, there was fight, heart and commitment to get over the line.

articles.title: Townsend hails Scotland's defence in Australia 'arm wrestle'
articles.summary: Scotland's Nations Championship win over Australia was far from a classic, but head coach Gregor Townsend says it was one of his side's best defensive performances in recent years.
body: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend hailed his team's defensive efforts after they edged past Australia in a Nations Championship "arm wrestle" at Murrayfield.
Off the back of being dismantled by New Zealand last weekend, in which they failed to score a second half point, the spotlight fell on Scotland's leaky defence.
But on a chilly and damp Edinburgh day where physicality was king, they delivered a much-needed win and showed they are capable of winning ugly.
Max Jorgensen's late converted try gave the Wallabies hope, and with the clock in the red, the visitors broke from their own half.

articles.title: Much still to do on F1 diversity - Hamilton
articles.summary: British Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton outlines three steps the sport must take to improve its diversity.
body: Lewis Hamilton says there is "much still to do" when it comes to increasing diversity in Formula 1.
The seven-time champion has used a report published on the five-year anniversary of establishing his Mission 44 charity, external to demand three key steps from the sport.
The campaign seeks to increase the representation of black people, women and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds in F1.
The report recognises that all parts of the industry have made steps to increase diversity.
